steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of water to a boil; add zucchini slices and cook until tender; drain well.
Heat olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat; stir in onion and garlic and cook until onion is tender, about 2 minutes.
Combine zucchini, onion, and garlic in a 9x12-inch casserole dish; pour marinara sauce on top and stir well. Top with mozzarella cheese.
Bake in preheated oven until zucchini slices are heated through and cheese is bubbly, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Zucchini Parmesan
raw_recipe.description: This easy zucchini Parmesan is a comforting casserole dish with layers of zucchini, marinara sauce, and cheese, baked until bubbling and delicious.
raw_recipe.name: Zucchini Parmesan

review.reviewBody:
I had made this on Saturday, did not soften the zucchini as directed but saute
them with the onions and garlic, added fresh sliced mushrooms, transferred to baking dish, layering as I did this and
sprinkled on Parmesan Cheese, 3 slices of
Julianne Swiss Cheese, and Mozzerella cheese with a 1/3 jar of Bertolli mushroom spagetti sauce with Merlot. It was just enough and it was just right. If you let it set after baking like lasagna it will absorb the water from the
sauce. Also I had sprinkle bread crumbs on the top before baking. Will be making
this again and again. Very good. Thank
you. forgot I had also added fresh basil 
from the garden.

I wanted to make zucchini parmesan with the bounty of zucchini from our garden, but was short on time. I found this recipe, and it was great. I call it "mock zucchini parmesan" since it isn't the traditional breaded and fried. Based on other reviews, I did skip the par boiling, and instead sautéed them in olive oil with garlic and onion before layering them in the pan. I sprinkled some bread crumbs before adding the mozzarella and parmesan cheeses. I topped it off with homemade marinara sauce from my freezer, and baked for 30-40 minutes at 350. Easier than breading and frying, and everyone loved it!

I made it a faster and easier way because I have fibromyalgia and can’t stand for long..
I grow my own zucchini so they are pretty big. 
I just sliced them in rounds and sprayed a few cookie sheets with non-stick spray. Then I just drizzled a tiny bit of olive oil on zucchini and sprinkled with seasoned Italian bread crumbs and spices and grated Asiago cheese on them and popped them in the oven. No frying, no eggs, no mess. Cooked until soft about 20 min. 
Pulled them out and they are ready to layer. Never frying again!! I mix seasonings in my ricotta with 1 egg. 
Made a meat sauce with fresh garlic and onions. 
Layer everything . Added grated Asiago between all layers too for flavor. We like it better then Parmesan or Romano. I buy a wedge at Trader Joe’s! Yum!!

My recipe is similar: 
1 each: small zucchini & small summer squash, 1/4-inch disc-sliced; 1-14-oz can Italian stewed tomatoes, chopped; 4, 1/4-inch slices fresh Mozzarella, cubed or not;1 t Italian seasoning. Layer squashes into a loaf pan. Stir in tomatoes with juices. Top with Mozzarella, then seasoning. Bake 350*/25 minutes. If necessary, brown top under broiler.

Everyone in my family really liked this, especially my husband. Like many reviewers I sauted the zucchini with the onion. I used tongs to remove the zucchini and a slotted spoon the rest of the veggies, in order to avoid excess moisture. I added finally diced carrots to the saute and a little feta to the cheese and baked at 350 for 30 minutes, allowing it to set for 10 minutes after soak up extra juices. It wasn't sloppy or runny at all, just perfect! It's the perfect recipe to use up left over mozzarella or pasta sauce.

I made this recipe, but sauteed the onion and zucchini til a bit soft with 2 tsp chopped garlic and a few shakes of dry Italian Seasoning & black pepper, then stirred in Nightshade-Free Marinara Sauce & heated a bit. Then I spooned the vegetable mixture into an Olive Oil Sprayed 9x13 pan, added Italian Bread Crumbs to cover, and then covered the dish with grated Italian Parmesan Cheese, and added shredded Jack Cheese on top. I baked the casserole for 25 minutes at 325 degrees F. in a convection oven. The casserole was not runny. This casserole dish gave me the flavor of Eggplant Parmesan without the Nightshades! ( As I have advanced in age, Nightshades have caused me more and more pain, even in minute amounts.) I am so thankful to find a substitute for Eggplant in one of my favorite Italian dinners! My husband liked it too.

Delicious! I also dipped zucchini (cut in half then sliced lengthwise around the core in order to remove seeds) in eggs, then plain breadcrumbs, drizzled some olive oil on top and baked at 450 for 10 mns each side. Layered using mozzarella, the sautéed onion and garlic drizzled in between along with thick sauce. 350 for additional 20 mns. Perfect..not mushy or watery.

This is the best zucchini I have found. I sauteed the zucchini with the onions and garlic, when done drained it in a colander to remove as much moisture as possible. I had more zucchini then the recipe called for so I layered it with the sauce and cheese. I used an entire can of Hunts Pasta sauce and 2 cups to mozzarella. I baked it at 375 for about 30 minutes. The more cheese the better for hubby. After making it we had something else for dinner and heated it up the next night. It was awesome....flavored through and mine didn't have any excess moisture. Will make this again & again &again.....

I sauteed the zucchini, onions and garlic instead of boiling. I used about 1/4 of a jar of marinara and three sliced fresh tomatoes. (instead of a whole jar). Also added fresh basil. 

It was lovely and I will make it again. 

Thank you Mary Jo!

I will definitely make it again. I changed it like many others that I read reviews on. I steamed the zucchini in a steamer on the stove so it did not become watery like some I read. I also used ground turkey and fried it up with the onion and garlic with salt and garlic powder. I added canned mushrooms then when it was cooked I added the sauce and simmered it some. Then I layered starting with the sauce then zucchini then the mozzarella like a lasagna. Baked it and it turned out great. My family loved it.

Not sure why this is titled Zucchini Parmesan when there’s no parmesan in the recipe, only mozzarella. As others have noted, consistency was a bit soupy, even after baking for another 5 minutes and under the broiler briefly, so I served with a slotted spoon. I parboiled the zucchini for 1 minute and then drained, since this was going into the oven for another 20 minutes. I used Classico® Sausage, Peppers, Onions marinara, so there was a little meat added, and I felt this needed both salt and pepper. I’d recommend that you use a marinara that you really like. Zucchini is very neutral in flavor, and what you taste most is the sauce. This ended up tasting pretty good, the zucchini was tender but not mushy, and the sauce and cheese were tasty.
It was easy dish to make and very tasty.
Sautéed added peppers and mushrooms

I made this for the first time tonight; my husband loved it! The only change I made was to saute the zucchini rather than boiling it. I baked it uncovered to avoid excess liquid. This one is a keeper!
Good recipe. These modern varieties of Zucchinni have almost no seeds even when allow to grow large.

My family and I loved it!! It's quite filling. I made it by the book this time. But next time, I'll probably brown some turkey sausage with Italian seasoning and add it to the spaghetti sauce. Mainly just to add protein, but I think the flavor added would be interesting as well.
It was really tasty. Was a little soupy. Maybe I used too much sauce. I added mushrooms and mozzarella and parmesan cheeses as well. I also added a dash of Italian seasoning.
Made this for my pregnant wife and it was great,gotta love those cravings you get when pregnan...

We loved this dish. I changed it because I used what I had on hand.

I used a three cheese Mexican blend instead of Mozzarella, and used a jar of 
pizza sauce in place of spaghetti sauce.

It was delicious!!!
Awesome, made it once in the oven and once on the grill
